nodes.text: @GavManB @glurcher @ShaunLintern The at risk groups are also offered Covid vaccines

nodes.author: GavManB
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @glurcher @ShaunLintern Yes and that's it in the UK. Doesn't stop you getting it or spreading it though.

nodes.author: stone3Clare
nodes.text: @GavManB @thatsnotmine125 @glurcher @ShaunLintern tbh, nowhere near enough people in you are offered covid vaccines - it’s very restricted groups. And even many of them don’t take them

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @GavManB @glurcher @ShaunLintern Correct, stops you going to hospital in lots of instances, and does reduce likelihood of infection and spreading it. Keeping infected people out of hospitals is important.

nodes.author: GavManB
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @glurcher @ShaunLintern Which they don't do, they barely test people and then have next to zero infection control.

nodes.author: GavManB
nodes.text: @thatsnotmine125 @glurcher @ShaunLintern It'll keep most out of hospital yes, it will not stop the spread.

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @GavManB @glurcher @ShaunLintern Well by virtue of having less infected people in hospitals the spread would be impacted. But I don’t know the answer really, there aren’t enough side rooms to isolate everyone infectious, staff aren’t paid to be off with URI unless poorly.

nodes.author: GavManB
nodes.text:
@thatsnotmine125 @glurcher @ShaunLintern Masks, HEPA. You know PPE.

Another thing causing issues is the staff getting sick from having no infection control. Long term sick is way up.

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @GavManB @glurcher @ShaunLintern They’ll have PPE and many A&Es are masking. But this has been an issue even when I worked in A&E and it’s extremely hard to change given layouts, policies and so on. Do you have any studies on HEPA in A&E? That would be interesting!

nodes.author: GavManB
thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @GavManB @glurcher @ShaunLintern Yes, that doesn’t surprise me - I wonder what costs more staff testing and taking paid time off, or staff being at work with infections?

nodes.author: thatsnotmine125
nodes.text: @GavManB @glurcher @ShaunLintern Vaccines very much keep infected people out of hospitals.
